The building on the drawings stopped existing years ago.

Every facility drifts. A wall moves, a duct gets rerouted, a machine is replaced, and nobody updates the set. By the time you need to plan a change, the documentation you are working from is a guess — and guesses get priced as rework.

We remove the guess. A scanner on site captures millions of measured points, which become a single registered model of the building as it stands today. Accurate, dimensioned, and ready to design against.

01 / capture

We scan on site

The scanner works from a series of set positions, capturing the space in full 360°. We work around production rather than stopping it, and most spaces are covered in a single visit.

02 / register

Scans become one model

Individual scans are aligned into a single coordinate system and checked for deviation, so every measurement in the finished dataset relates to every other one.

03 / deliver

You get usable files

Registered point cloud, a Revit or CAD model built to the level of detail you need, and a 2D set of plans, sections and elevations. Yours to keep and reuse.

Three industries, one problem.

Manufacturing, mechanical services and design practices all hit the same wall: you cannot plan a change to a building you have not measured. What differs is the deliverable each one needs at the end.

01

Manufacturing

Retool the line without shutting it down.

Before you move a press, add a conveyor or drop in a new cell, you need to know what is genuinely in the way — structure, services, clearances, floor levels. Not what the layout drawing says was in the way a decade ago.

We scan the plant while it runs, then give you a model you can test-fit equipment into before it ships. Interferences get found on a screen instead of on a Saturday shutdown.

  • Equipment fit and clearance checks
  • Conveyor and work cell layouts
  • Floor flatness and slab levels
  • Structural steel verification
  • Crane and access envelopes
  • Line relocation and expansion

02

HVAC & Mechanical

See the mechanical space before you price the job.

Risers, plenums and ceiling voids are where estimates go wrong. They are congested, undocumented, and awkward to survey by hand — so routing gets decided from a ladder and a tape, and the difference shows up as a change order.

Scanning captures every duct, hanger and pipe run exactly where it sits. New services get routed against measured space, and clashes surface during coordination rather than during install.

  • Duct and pipe route verification
  • Plant room and riser surveys
  • Clash detection against new services
  • Ceiling void and plenum capture
  • Equipment replacement access routes
  • Retrofit and efficiency upgrades

03

Architecture & Design

Start design from measured reality.

Renovation, adaptive reuse and additions all begin with an existing conditions survey, and the quality of that survey sets the ceiling on everything after it. Inherited drawings are a liability dressed up as a head start.

We deliver a registered point cloud and a modelled set that drops straight into Revit, so schemes are drawn over the building as it actually stands — including the parts that are out of square.

  • Existing conditions surveys
  • Revit and CAD as-built models
  • Facade and elevation capture
  • Adaptive reuse and heritage work
  • Plans, sections and ceiling plans
  • Coordination sets for consultants
